proposals.title: Points on the table: every skill priced in SAT points
proposals.what:
SERVER: F4 adds progress.points(learner). For each of the 19 skills:
pts = expected questions on one 44-question section × the student's miss rate × points per question.
- Expected questions: the BLUEPRINT domain share × the skill's share within its domain, from a fixed constant built from College Board Question Bank counts per skill (e.g. Linear functions 170 of Algebra's 615; the teardown lists them all).
- Miss rate: 1 − recent accuracy at a test-like mix of difficulty, pulled toward the domain mean while evidence is under 10 answers.
- Points per question: the slope of scoring.ANCHORS at the student's band, about 13 between 480 and 620 and about 14 above.
It returns {topic, pts, per_test, miss_rate, evidence}.

ME SKILLS CARD:
- A seg sort, 'By points on the table · By domain', defaulting to points.
- Each row adds '≈ 18 pts' in DM Mono and 'about 3 questions a test · you miss 45%'.
- Header: 'About 60 points on the table · your top 3 skills hold 34'.
- Footer pill: 'Practise the top 3 · 10'.

TARGET POPOVER: states the target in questions: '700 ≈ 37 of 44 right; you're near 31. The 6 you're most likely missing are in Circles, Probability and Nonlinear functions.'

ELSEWHERE: Up next, the palette's Skills group and the coach's tie-breaks order by pts. A Help anchor, 'How points on the table is worked out', states the caveat 'an estimate; bands are ±70'.

STUDENT DOES: spends the next hour on the skill worth the most points, not on the one that feels weakest.
MOVES THE SCORE BECAUSE: a skill with 1 question a test at 30% accuracy is worth less than one with 4 questions at 70%. Pricing both in points makes that trade-off visible, and working by marginal points is the fastest route to a higher scaled score.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's domain cards read '13% · 13% of test section, 1-8 questions' (confusing copy, per the live walk). Their per-question payload has no skill, and their Subject Performance block is empty on a new account. Nothing tells a TopTierPrep student where the points are.
proposals.needs: F4 progress.points plus the R16 band; one constant table of per-skill test shares; F2 palette order; S7 and the coach may weight by it; S6 Results can show the same column.

proposals.title: Log a mistake, rebuilt: paste the question, or log a whole Bluebook test
proposals.what:
(A) PASTE. The first field of the quick sheet's Log a mistake tab is 'Paste or type the question'. POST /api/types/match {text}:
- strips the numbers and single-letter variables, then tokenises;
- ranks templates by TF-IDF cosine against fingerprints built at startup from the survey's 18 stems per template (stdlib Counter and math, no new dependency);
- returns the top 4 {template, skill, score, example}.
They render as 'Like this one?' cards, each showing a generated example from the reserved 900000+ seeds. The student taps one, or chooses 'None of these' and falls back to the specified skill → type path. Then come 'What went wrong?' (that type's reasons) and 'Where was it?'.

(B) A WHOLE TEST. A 'Log a Bluebook test' tab:
1. Date and score, which go through S3's add_outside_score onto the trend.
2. Two 22-cell grids (Module 1, Module 2). The student taps each question they missed and gives it a skill from a compact 19-chip picker (Bluebook's review lists each question's skill).
3. Submit builds a 'Bluebook follow-up' set: 2 fresh questions per missed skill, drawn from that skill's types the student has missed before or never met.
Misses in that set open named traps as usual, and the set becomes Up next's first item.

(C) FIX PATH for every logged mistake:
1. The example, with the chosen misconception's option highlighted as 'this is the trap', and the rationale.
2. One fresh repair question.
3. The R9 check-ins at 3, 10 and 30 days.

STUDENT DOES: turns every official practice test and school worksheet into drilled mistakes in under a minute, without having to learn our taxonomy.
MOVES THE SCORE BECAUSE: official tests are the most test-like practice there is, but most students read the score and move on. Turning each miss into a named, spaced repair keeps what the test taught. Matching by text removes the classifying step that stops students logging at all, and the follow-up set names the exact misconception behind a miss logged only by skill.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's floating button captures only vocabulary words ('Add your own word'), and it covers Next in QBank sessions. Nothing on TopTierPrep takes in a Bluebook test or a Math miss from outside the site.
proposals.needs: F5 /api/types, /api/types/{t}/example and /api/mistakes/log (already specified), plus a new /api/types/match and the survey stems kept per template; S3 add_outside_score; F4 R9 check-ins; F2 quick sheet tabs (R29); S10 Review's 'Logged by you · Bluebook' chip.

proposals.title: Pace profile: where your minutes go, and the drill that fixes each case
proposals.what:
SERVER: F4 adds progress.pace(learner). Over the last 60 days, per skill with ≥ 5 timed answers: the median seconds on right answers and the accuracy. It reads attempts.ms from practice and the tests' qstate ms, which record_paper carries into attempts.ms (R7).
It also returns a module forecast: the sum of each skill's median time over a blueprint-mixed 22-question module, e.g. 'At your pace a module takes 38:40 of 35:00: about 3 questions left blank.'

ME PACE CARD: a 2×2 quadrant chart. x is median time against the 1:35 pace; y is accuracy against the student's own mean. Each skill is a labelled glyph dot, with a hidden data table. Each quadrant has a label and one action:
- Slow and right, 'You know it, slowly': Speed drill, 8 questions at 70 s each (custom clock) on that skill.
- Fast and wrong, 'Rushing': Careful set, 8 untimed, with the top habit's tell (proposal 2) shown above each stem.
- Slow and wrong, 'Time sink': the skill joins a 'Skip and come back' list for test day, read by Tests' test-day checklist and the runner's pace guide. Offer 'Learn it untimed · 8'.
- Fast and right, 'Banked': keep warm.
The header carries the forecast and a pill, 'Pacing drill · half a module (11 q · 17:25)', at SAT pace with a blueprint mix.

STUDENT DOES: runs speed drills on the skills they know but solve slowly, and walks into the test knowing which kinds of question to skip first.
MOVES THE SCORE BECAUSE: in a timed module, a 3-minute solve costs two other questions. Accuracy gains are wasted if the student can't finish, and pacing can only be trained once the student sees, per skill, where the minutes go.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep records time only per attempt inside a QBank session (the Attempt History modal). Its 'Time analysis' card exists only for contests and was empty. Its score report payload carries no time at all. Nothing tells a TopTierPrep student whether they would finish a module.
proposals.needs: F4 R7 (test ms into attempts); F1 a quadrant scatter in charts.js; F5 drill timed/minutes; S5 test-day checklist and pace guide read the skip list; proposal 2 tells.

proposals.title: Calibration: the mistakes you make while sure
proposals.what:
DATA: attempts.guess (practice 'I'm guessing', R8) and qstate.conf (the tests' Sure/Unsure/Guess). Add a prefs key `confidence`, default off, so practice can tag Sure/Unsure/Guess in the workspace strip (K, already in the runner map).

ME CARD 'When you're sure': three bars, each with n, for example Sure 84% right (212), Unsure 58% (64), Guess 29% (31, chance 25%). Each bar gets one generated advice line when it applies:
- Unsure accuracy ≥ 55%: 'Your unsure answers are usually right. On test day, answer and move on.'
- Guess accuracy ≤ 30%: 'Your guesses are at chance. Eliminate two first: your strikes were on wrong options 88% of the time' (from qstate.struck, when present).

CONFIDENT ERRORS: misconceptions chosen while Sure, or in practice while not marked a guess, at least twice. Example: 'Used the diameter as the radius · chosen sure 3 times'. Each has 'Fix · 3' (a trap drill) and ranks first among mistakes in Up next. The summary's stats add sure_right, unsure_right and guess_right.

STUDENT DOES: gives extra attention to the few errors they believe are right, and stops re-working unsure answers that are usually correct.
MOVES THE SCORE BECAUSE: a confident error is the one a student never double-checks on test day. It is also the easiest to correct once shown (the hypercorrection effect). Calibrated students spend review time and test-day checking time where it pays.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no confidence input anywhere, and its QBank allows unlimited retries, which makes its accuracy meaningless (teardown weakness 2).
proposals.needs: F4 R8 guess column and the summary aggregates; S5 and F3 conf in qstate and a practice confidence toggle in the strip; F4 prefs key `confidence`; proposal 1 ordering.

proposals.title: Time-boxed start: 'I have 5 / 15 / 30 minutes'
proposals.what:
WHERE: the sidebar Today card, the quick sheet header and the phone menu sheet's Up next row all get a chip row, 'Got time? 5 · 15 · 30 min'. The palette parses '15 min', '15m' and 'half hour'.

SERVER: POST /api/drill {source: 'next', minutes: 15, timed: from the stage (proposal 8)}. It sets count = floor(minutes × 60 / 95). The set is filled from next.queue in order: check-ins due, confident errors, the mistakes worth the most points, one weak skill, one keep-warm skill. practice.interleave orders it so no two consecutive questions share a skill.

SESSION: a box clock reads '12:40 left of your 15'. At zero the current question finishes, then the summary shows with Up next as its primary.

STUDENT DOES: uses the 10 minutes before class or on the bus on the right mix, instead of skipping the day.
MOVES THE SCORE BECAUSE: short, frequent, interleaved retrieval of due material beats occasional long blocks. A correctly sized session one tap away means more study days, and every minute goes to what is due.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's QBank volume choice is 10/20/30/40/50/All, with no link to time and no mix. Its daily goal ('2 Hours') gives no way to spend 10 minutes well.
proposals.needs: Proposal 1's next.queue; F5 drill source 'next' that fills from the queue (practice.interleave already exists); F2 chips and palette parsing; proposal 8 for the clock.

proposals.title: Practice settings that follow your stage, from learning to test conditions
proposals.what:
PREF: a new key `stage_auto`, default true once an exam date exists. The stage comes from the plan's phase (plan_days.phase), or from days to the exam when there is no plan:
- Learn (> 42 days): untimed, instant feedback, repairs next, rationale on miss, adaptive tiers.
- Build (42 to 21 days): SAT pace clock on sets, instant feedback, grid-in share at the test's level.
- Test (21 to 7 days): SAT pace, feedback at the end on mixed sets of 10 or more, repairs at the end, a module each week.
- Final week: check-ins and open mistakes only, no new types, one full section 3 to 5 days out, nothing new on the eve.

UI.prefs() returns each value with its source, 'stage' or 'yours'. On the Learning preferences card and in Settings › Practice, each row the stage sets reads 'Set by your stage: Build · 34 days to Nov 7', with Change. Change pins that key as 'yours' and adds a 'Back to stage' reset.

BANNER: on the day the stage changes: 'Test stage starts today: sets now run at SAT pace with the key at the end.' [Why?] opens Help.

STUDENT DOES: practises under test conditions in the final weeks without having to remember to switch, and learns with immediate feedback early on.
MOVES THE SCORE BECAUSE: immediate feedback speeds early learning. Timed practice with delayed feedback in the final weeks builds the pacing and unaided retrieval the test demands. Most self-studiers never make the switch.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Learning Preferences are static selects (Practice Mode Timed/Untimed, Difficulty Adaptive/Fixed), and its plan data model has no phase. A TopTierPrep student in the final week practises exactly as in week one unless they change a select by hand.
proposals.needs: F4 prefs.py key stage_auto and the stage resolution; S7 plan phase in /api/shell.plan; S4 and S5 already read the merged prefs; S1 row captions.

proposals.title: Precision you can see, and a 12-question Sharpen check
proposals.what:
SKILL ROWS: when a skill has fewer than 10 answers behind it (the evidence count board() already has), its mastery bar gets a faint uncertainty extension and the row reads 'rough · 4 answers'. Otherwise it reads 'measured · 26 answers'. /api/me/summary adds evidence per skill.

SKILLS CARD HEADER: '7 skills are still rough. Sharpen · 12 questions · ~19 min'. The button sends POST /api/drill {source: 'probe', topics: the 4 to 6 rough skills ranked by test share × uncertainty, count 12, adaptive true, feedback 'end', repairs 'end'}.

SUMMARY (S4): says what changed. 'Probability: rough → Learning (the coach now includes it). Circles: rough → Strong (the coach will skip it).'

COACH AND UP NEXT: a rough skill gets one probe before it is assigned a full set. A new student's Skills card offers Sharpen and the diagnostic side by side.

STUDENT DOES: spends 19 minutes measuring before weeks of practice, and can trust the coach's picks.
MOVES THE SCORE BECAUSE: coaching is only as good as its measurement. With a wrong picture of weak and strong, sessions go to skills the student already knows while real gaps go unmet. Probing the least-measured, highest-weight skills gets the most information per question.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's 'Difficulty Level: Adaptive' has no visible model behind it. Its estimate shows 'LOW CONFIDENCE' in red with no way to fix it, and its subject block is empty until tests are taken.
proposals.needs: F4 evidence in board() and in the summary; F5 source 'probe' with feedback 'end'; S4 the summary's 'what changed' block; F4 the coach reads evidence.

proposals.title: Every number says how to move it
proposals.what:
WHAT OPENS: every stat on Me, the Today card and the nav tooltips opens a UI.pop popover on tap or focus: streak, accuracy, mastery bars, types met, rank, band, points on the table and check-ins.

THE POPOVER has three parts:
1. How it's worked out: one line, plus a link to its Help anchor.
2. Your numbers: the inputs behind it, e.g. 'last 10 Circles answers: 7 right, 3 of them hard'.
3. What moves it: the next threshold, computed on the server, with a Start button where there is one to start.

WHAT MOVES IT, per number:
- Mastery: '2 more right on medium or hard reaches Strong'. Found by simulating answers appended to mastery_of until the next UI.masteryWord boundary; it is a pure function, so this is cheap.
- Streak: 'Answer 1 today to make it 7'.
- Types met: '4 unmet in Circles · Practise unmet'.
- Rank: '12 more right this week passes #127'.
- Band: 'A module with 2 more right moves the band about 30'.

/api/me/summary adds levers {key: {how, inputs, next, drill?}}.

STUDENT DOES: sees the concrete next step behind every number, and taps it.
MOVES THE SCORE BECAUSE: a goal feels reachable when the gap is small and stated (the goal-gradient effect). A student who knows exactly what moves a bar stops grinding random questions.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's numbers come unexplained: Global Rank 128 with no contests played and no stated basis, a 7-segment domain bar with confusing copy, 'LOW CONFIDENCE' with no reason, and a target modal that states the wrong current score.
proposals.needs: F4 pure functions (mastery_of, days, practice_rank) for the simulations; F1 UI.pop; S1 summary levers; S8 the rank gap.

proposals.title: Offline pack for the bus
proposals.what:
GETTING THE PACK: on the installed app only, the menu sheet has 'Save 30 questions for offline', and the pack refreshes nightly while online. GET /api/pack?n=30 returns practice items from next.queue with keys and rationales. Every item passes deps.access, so never a live-test item and never today's challenge. The pack lives in IndexedDB.

OFFLINE: the practice session runs from the pack in practice mode with instant feedback. Answers queue in UI.saveQueue with their original `at` and ms, and replay on reconnect. The server re-grades each answer from (template, seed) and ignores the client's verdict, and progress.record accepts a client `at` up to 7 days old.

THE SHELL: shows 'Offline · 22 questions saved · Practise' in place of the offline error banner.

STUDENT DOES: practises in dead time without a signal (commute, lunch).
MOVES THE SCORE BECAUSE: it adds short retrieval sessions every week. Phones are where students study, and a dropped connection currently ends practice.

parity_gaps.spec_says: §2.2–2.3: a 248px sidebar that collapses to a 68px rail (toggle or [); grouped links with metas (counts, New, Resume, #rank); an active pill.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs has the same shape: a ~220px sidebar, a toggle to a ~60px rail, an active pill. Our badges say what is waiting, but both still hand the student a list of places and leave the choice to them.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Put Up next (proposal 1) at the top of the sidebar and rail: title, reason, minutes and points. N starts it on every page, and every session end chains into it.

parity_gaps.spec_says: §2.6: avatar, name, email or 'This device only', role line; Profile, Settings, Sign in, Pair, Join a class, Shortcuts, Help, Send feedback, Sign out. Esc closes it.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs has avatar, name, email, My Profile, Send feedback and Sign out. Fixing Esc and adding links is housekeeping; it does nothing for studying.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Profiles on a shared device: 'Switch student' keeps up to 4 learner codes in localStorage satf.profiles, each with avatar, name and today's minutes. One-tap switch with no sign-out, plus 'Add a student' and Remove. Siblings or a tutor's laptop stop mixing answers into one code, which would otherwise corrupt mastery, mistakes and the coach's picks. Add a 'Saved · synced 2 min ago' line.

parity_gaps.spec_says: §1 and §5: a 6-digit email code (needs SMTP, open question 5), a pairing code approved on the first device, and a device code.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs is Google one-tap. Ours is safer and has no wall, but a returning student on a new device switches to the mail app and types 6 digits, roughly 30–60 s, so it is no faster than theirs. Without SMTP, email doesn't work at all.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Passkeys (WebAuthn). 'Save with a passkey' registers a platform credential in a new table passkeys(id, learner, public_key, sign_count, label, created). On a new device, sign-in is one Face ID or fingerprint tap, synced through iCloud Keychain or Google Password Manager. No SMTP, phishing-proof, and email codes stay as recovery. It needs py_webauthn, or about 150 lines of ES256 verification with cryptography.

parity_gaps.spec_says: §3.1 + R31: a 2×4 grid (Streak, Answered, Accuracy, Study time, Tests, Mistakes fixed, Words, Rating), each with a sub-line and a link.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs is 2×2: Streak/Tests/Solved/Vocab. Ours has more tiles, but they are the same kind: volume counts that say how much was done, not whether the score is moving.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Lead with outcome tiles: SINCE YOU STARTED ('+80 · 480–560 → 560–640', first scored sitting to the current estimate), POINTS ON THE TABLE ('≈ 60 · top 3 skills 34') and CHECK-INS PASSED ('12 of 14 still fixed'). Volume moves to the sub-lines. Every tile opens its 'what moves it' popover (proposal 11).

parity_gaps.spec_says: §3.1: an initial or one of 19 topic glyphs; no photo, for minors' privacy.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs uploads a photo. Ours is a privacy-safe stand-in for the same feature, and just as inert.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Earned glyphs: a skill's glyph unlocks as an avatar when that skill reaches Strong, and a domain frame when every skill in the domain is Strong. The picker shows locked glyphs with 'Reach Strong in Circles', so the avatar shows mastery and gives a reason to finish a skill.

parity_gaps.spec_says: §3.2 + R3: practice rank by right answers over a rolling 7 days, among everyone, the same exam date, and each class.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs is Global and Country rank. Ours picks a better cohort on stated terms but still ranks volume (open question 12). Grinding easy questions wins, and a weaker student who is improving fast sits near the bottom.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A growth rank: among students who started in the same band (first scored sitting ±40) and sit the same exam date, rank by estimated points gained, or mastery gained, over 30 days. 'You've improved faster than 72% of students who started at 480–560.' Shown at n ≥ 20 (R16's rule), with right answers kept as a second metric. It rewards learning, not volume, and gives every level a race it can win.

parity_gaps.feature: Study goals: target, exam date and countdown
parity_gaps.spec_says: §3.3: a target bar with '+100 to go'; a target popover (slider, chips); an exam-date popover of upcoming dates with 'in N days'; a countdown bar; daily and weekly goal bars; week dots; preferred time.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs has Target, Exam date with 'N days remaining', Daily, Weekly and Preferred time. Ours is synced and editable, which fixes their bugs, but it states the same facts: a number and days left, never whether that is realistic or what reaching it takes.

(b) The target in questions: '700 ≈ 37 of 44 right; you're near 31.' parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs is a per-subject performance block. Ours is more detailed but still a report card in syllabus order: it says where the student is weak, not what the weakness costs or how far the bar can be trusted.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Sort by points on the table (proposal 3). Add a precision whisker with 'rough · 4 answers' and the Sharpen probe (proposal 10), a 14-day trend arrow per skill, and a 'fading' marker on Strong skills untouched for 10+ days, with 'Keep warm · 3'.

parity_gaps.spec_says: §3.6: a range bar per sitting, a target line, an exam tick, tooltips and click-through to the report.

parity_gaps.spec_says: §3.11 + §9: '57 of 386 question types', with domain and topic bars and 'Practise types I haven't met'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It swaps their usage meters for a coverage meter, but a raw count weighs a rare type the same as one on every test, so '57 of 386' says little about readiness.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Weight coverage by how often a type appears on the test: 'Types that make up 80% of test questions: 41 of 60 met', with 'Meet the next most common type' first. The raw count moves to a second line, so coverage tracks the questions the student will actually see.

parity_gaps.feature: Classes: assign, due dates, attach working
parity_gaps.spec_says: §7: join by code; set, module or section assignments, fresh per student or the same for all; due dates, late status and attachments; a roster; a class misconception ranking; 'Assign a repair to these 9'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their bundle has create class, add students, assign, due dates and Attach file. Fresh numbers stop copying, but every student still gets the same content.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A third Questions option, 'Tailored': on the assigned skills, each student's set starts with their own open traps and due check-ins, then their least-met types, then fresh questions, with one count and due date for everyone. The teacher's detail shows 'had 3 of their own mistakes · fixed 2' per student, so one assignment does the right work for 24 different students.
